quotes.how: parsed with scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs's own `intentCriteria` routine, extracted from that file and run over the intent, so every criterionText below is the intent's own text and not a paraphrase; scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs compares character for character, and scripts/stability-capture.test.mjs reddens on a row whose criterion differs from the intent by one character and on a row whose criterionCharacters is off by one

why: No row is required, and the list therefore names no driver, no instance and no verdict path: scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs refuses a list with no required row that names a driver, so naming one would be the opposite defect.

The reason is not convenience. A required row must name the driver a control-ai-browsers run expression takes to the wave gate, and that driver must return the gate's four readings - toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext - with the required rows together citing drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext, because that is the reading set the overlay driver produces. This milestone's readings are a boolean emission the page published, the page's own performance.now() at attach and at that emission, one entry per profiler event the frame recorded, and the named absences a boolean stream and a Set<number> force - none of which an element's rect or dev context can produce. Naming spikes/probes/overlay-pick.js as their driver would make the gate return overlay measurements for stability criteria, which is the re-cut N6 forbids; a stability driver does not exist in this repository and this task may not add one.

The portal is not lost by that ruling: it is the subject the reasons name, and it is where this milestone is least settled - the intent's first open question is whether the portal's zoneless target is permanently stable, so a portal-backed verdict would be evidence about the page's silence rather than about the reader that refuses to read stability out of it. Every row above names the artefact that carries it and the exact command that proves it.

claims.criterionText: The stability state is reported for each inspected page from that page's own `ApplicationRef.isStable`, reached by the injector read the agent already performs for `Router` and from nothing else: on the counter fixture's `/resource-states`, whose never-settling `resource()` takes a pending task for the page's lifetime (`spikes/ng222-app/src/app/resource-states.ts:61,67-71`; `_resource-chunk.mjs:404`), the finding reports the app unstable and names the emission it read; on a page whose `isStable` has emitted `true` it reports stable from that emission; and a page exposing no reachable `ApplicationRef`, or an `isStable` that cannot be subscribed, is cannot-tell with the named absence `no-stability-observable`, never stable and never a zero count.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m043-stability.json (reach.walk: the five steps the agent already performs for Router - ng.getInjector, ɵgetInjectorResolutionPath, ɵgetInjectorProviders, the record whose token.name matches, injector.get(token); reach.subjects.withToken: reachedBy "ApplicationRef", absence null, getterReads 1, subscriptions 1, state read from the emission; reach.subjects.withoutToken: reachedBy null, absence "no-stability-observable", state "cannot-tell"; page.route "/resource-states", page.state "unstable", page.stateFor "the page's lifetime"; record.frame and record.snapshot: the section both records carry) -> extension/agent-main.js:2285 (var STABILITY_TOKEN_NAME = 'ApplicationRef';), :2388 (stream = appRef.isStable;), :2443 (stabilityField), :1052 and :1442 (the section on the frame record and on the initial snapshot) -> extension/stability-narrator.js (stateOf: the emission's own value decides, and the record's own absence word decides cannot-tell)
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause is answered rather than dodged. A portal route is an Angular page, so it could in principle produce this criterion's stable half - and that is exactly why the ruling is stated here instead of left to silence: no `control-ai-browsers run` driver in this repository reads `ApplicationRef.isStable`. The one driver the wave gate owns returns the overlay's four readings (toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor, noDevContext), so a row naming it would make the gate return an element's rect for a stability claim, which is the re-cut N6 forbids; and whether the portal's zoneless target is ever unstable has never been read, which is the intent's own first open question. A portal-backed verdict would therefore name a driver this repository does not have. What carries the claim is research/raw/m043-stability.json, where the walk, the two subjects and the unstable page are each derived, joined by extension/stability-narrator.js. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/stability-narrator.test.mjs", whose E1 pin renders the state from the emission alone and whose E2 pin renders no-stability-observable for both unreachable causes, with node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/stability-measure.test.mjs" holding the reach to the agent's own source.

claims.criterionText: The settle time is a reading the page published or a named absence, never an inference: when the stability read emits a change from unstable to stable while the surface is attached, the finding reports the time between the page's own `performance.now()` reading at attach and its reading when `true` arrived, and reports a measured `0` as `0`; a page already stable at attach, a page whose transition happened before attach, and a page that never settles each render the absence `no-settle-observed` with no time and no duration, and no interval taken from the record's quiet tail ever stands in for one.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m043-stability.json (transition.subjects['unstable-then-stable'].settle: { state: "settled", at: 1008, sinceAttachMs: 7 } against attachAt 1001; transition.subjects['stable-at-attach'].settle: { state: "settled", at: 1001, sinceAttachMs: 0 } with answer "no-transition-observed"; transition.alreadyStableAtAttach: a settle at attach is a reading and never a transition; transition.subjects['silent-stream'] and ['no-application-ref']: { state: "no-settle-observed" } with no time; transition.answer "no-transition-observed" and transition.producedOnAnInspectedPage false; record.snapshot.settle: { state: "no-settle-observed" }; page.loader: settles false) -> extension/stability-narrator.js (settleOf: settle.at minus attachAt, both published by the page, a measured 0 kept as 0, and no time field on the absence) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-stability.ts (the settle block prints 0 or the absence and nothing else)
claims.reason: This criterion's positive half needs a page whose last pending task ends after the read is attached, and no portal route has been driven with the read attached: the portal's zoneless target is the subject the intent's first open question names, and it may be permanently stable, in which case a portal drive would return no-settle-observed rather than the transition this criterion is written on. So the charter's portal clause reaches no portal fact that has been measured, and no `control-ai-browsers run` driver in this repository reads `isStable` at all - the gate's only driver returns the overlay's four readings, none of which carries a stability bit. What carries the claim is research/raw/m043-stability.json, which separates the three shapes (a transition of 7 ms measured by the mechanism, a settle at attach of 0 ms reported as a reading and never as a transition, and the named absence for both the silent and the unreachable subject) and names `transitionProducible: false` on a page. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/stability-narrator.test.mjs", whose E3 pin holds the measured zero, the absence with no time field and the interval to the page's own two readings; scripts/stability-capture.test.mjs drives two pages in one session and requires each page's own settle reading and no emission of one attributed to the other.

claims.criterionText: The work that ran while the app was unstable is reported as the frames the page recorded, and repetition is read from the frame's own `events` list and nothing else: two `TemplateUpdate` start/end pairs inside one `checks` row are reported as two passes over that component, a second `ChangeDetection` pair carrying `componentName: null` is reported as a second change-detection pass attributed to no component, and a frame holding one pair reports one; no per-view cycle count, no outstanding-work count and no pass the `events` list does not hold is ever reported.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m043-stability.json (repeats.templateUpdate: inOneCheckRow 2, starts 2, checkRowEvents [2,3,2,3], componentNames ["app-root"]; repeats.changeDetection: starts 2, nullComponentNames 4, inAnyCheckRow false; repeats.shape: one entry per recorded value, { type, pair, end, at, componentName }) -> extension/stability-narrator.js (readEvent and repeatsOf: one pass per start/end pair in the frame's own events, grouped per pair and per component, with no cycle count and no outstanding count anywhere in the answer) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-stability.ts (repeatsBlock: one line per pass the answer carried)
claims.reason: These facts are the frame's own events list, which only an agent attached to the page records: no `control-ai-browsers run` driver in this repository returns a frame, and the gate's only driver returns the overlay's four readings, so the charter's portal clause has no route whose facts this criterion names - a portal-backed verdict would be evidence about an element rather than about the work a frame recorded. The portal is named here rather than skipped because it was considered: a portal drive would have to run the page agent and read the record it dispatches, which is a different instrument from the one the wave gate owns, and no such driver exists. What carries the claim is research/raw/m043-stability.json's repeats block, re-derived at this head by driving the shipped agent, and extension/stability-narrator.js, whose repeat list is one entry per pair the frame recorded. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/stability-narrator.test.mjs", whose E5 pin renders two passes over one component from two template-update pairs in one checks row and one pass attributed to no component from a second ChangeDetection pair, and whose E6 pin renders no pass at all for a frame that recorded no paired work; scripts/panel-stability.test.mjs holds the pane's repeated-work block to the same list.

claims.criterionText: Every question the page cannot answer is cannot-tell with its own named absence and no guessed value: the cause is `no-cause-reported`, because `isStable` is a boolean stream (`_debug_node-chunk.mjs:13221-13222`); the outstanding items, their count, their kind and their owner are `no-outstanding-inventory`, because `PendingTasksInternal` holds a `Set<number>` whose `add()` takes no descriptor (`_pending_tasks-chunk.mjs:2304-2312`); the first item to settle and any per-item order are `no-settle-order`, because no timestamp and no settle time crosses any API; and no absence is ever filled from a task id, an epoch delta, a signal-graph label, a component name or a creation stack.
claims.artefact: research/raw/m043-stability.json (absences: the five entries that name the cause, the outstanding inventory and the settle order, each with the chunk anchor it rests on - _debug_node-chunk.mjs:13221-13222 for the boolean getter, _pending_tasks-chunk.mjs:2286 for the Set<number>, :2305 to :2316-2322 for add()/remove(); observable.pendingTasks.noPerItemOrder: ids only, no component, no label, no reason; observable.getter: one pipe(map(pending => !pending)) over a boolean) -> extension/stability-narrator.js (PERMANENT_ABSENCES, ABSENCE_ORDER and absencesOf: one named absence per unanswered question, each its own name and its own sentence, none rendered as a zero) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-stability.ts (one cell and one sentence per absence)
claims.reason: The portal is the subject on which every one of these absences is total rather than partial - it is the app whose pending-task set holds bare ids and whose isStable is a boolean - but an absence is not a driver's reading: no `control-ai-browsers run` driver in this repository returns a named absence, and the gate's only driver returns the overlay's four readings, so a portal-backed verdict would name a driver that cannot carry the answer. CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore has no portal route that renders the criterion's own fact, and the surface that does render it is served from apps/angular-ai-devtools, which inspects the page rather than being it. What carries the claim is research/raw/m043-stability.json, whose absences block quotes the installed chunks each absence rests on, and extension/stability-narrator.js, which mints no cause, no owner, no call site and no task id from a task id, an epoch delta, a signal-graph label or an opted-in creation stack. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/stability-narrator.test.mjs", whose E7 pin keeps the four absences distinct and each rendering alone and whose E8 pin keeps an app that opted into provideStabilityDebugging() at no-outstanding-inventory.

claims.criterionText: The panel surface renders the state, the settle time or its named absence, and the repeated-work reading, each in its own block, and renders nothing else: no sentence names a cause, no list names an outstanding item or its owner, no column orders work by settle time, the surface is registered in the route table that carries no stability route today (`apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/app.routes.ts:17-160`), and asked for a page it has no stability answer for it renders `no-stability-observable` rather than an empty table or an em dash.
claims.artefact: apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-stability.ts:404 (stabilityPanel(answer), three blocks in one order - the state, the settle reading, the repeated work - and one block and one sentence per named absence, with no cause, no outstanding item, no owner and no order) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/app.routes.ts:167 (path: 'stability', through the shared loadPanelDemo loader, a table that carried no stability route before this milestone) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-demo.ts (the stability loader key and the sample fact, which is the join's own answer for research/raw/m043-stability.json's record.frame beside the frame's own events) -> apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-demo.spec.ts:1567 and :1652 (E9)
claims.proves: node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-stability.test.mjs" and node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-routes.test.mjs" and npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test
claims.reason: This criterion is about the surface, and the surface is served from the panel rather than from any inspected page: no insurance-portal route renders it, and no portal route produces the DOM this criterion names, so the charter's portal clause has no portal fact to reach even though the criterion itself is proven. The panel is the only surface the intent declares, the route lives in the panel's own table, and the page the pane is driven against is the fixture's - which is a second reason a portal-backed verdict would measure the wrong subject. What carries the claim is apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-stability.ts rendered through the route registered in apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/app.routes.ts, with the demo's sample fact being the join's own answer for the recording rather than a value invented for the demo. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-stability.test.mjs", whose nine real mutants redden the pane's own pins by string - another state's text in a cell, a cause named in prose, an outstanding item listed with its owner, the settle absence rendered as an empty field, the repeated-work block omitted, a wall clock read for the interval, an interval taken from the settle time itself, an empty pane for a page nobody read and stable claimed for one - with scripts/panel-routes.test.mjs holding the route and its single loader and npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test carrying held-out E9 in panel-demo.spec.ts.

claims.criterionText: Stability is reported as a measurement and never as the absence of a report: a page whose change-detection record has gone silent but whose `isStable` reads `true` reports stable with the reading that says so, a page whose record is silent and whose stability was never read reports `no-stability-observable`, and no surface renders stable on the strength of a quiet interval, an empty finding set or the record's silence — the failure mode the roadmap's own risk line names (`.project/ROADMAP.md:1587`), measured in the agent's shape, which dispatches one snapshot at install and thereafter only frames (`extension/agent-main.js:566,1418-1448,1038-1060`).
claims.artefact: research/raw/m043-stability.json (transition.subjects['silent-stream']: state "idle", reading null, settle "no-settle-observed"; reach.subjects.withoutToken: state "cannot-tell", absence "no-stability-observable", reading null; record.silentFrame and record.absentFrame: the section as each record carries it; page.state "unstable" beside them; record.armedAt :1865 and :1870 with the initial snapshot at :1442 and the frames at :1052) -> extension/stability-narrator.js (stateOf: idle is not stable, cannot-tell is not stable, and the verdict is the emission's value and never the presence or absence of a frame; PERMANENT_ABSENCES) -> scripts/stability-capture.test.mjs (E11: two pages in one session, each answering its own state and its own settle reading)
claims.reason: This criterion is about the instrument's own failure mode rather than about a page, and no insurance-portal route produces a record, a frame or a verdict from silence, so the charter's portal clause has no portal fact to reach - a portal-backed verdict would still be evidence about a page rather than about the reader that refuses to read stability out of a quiet interval. The portal is named here because it is the page most likely to be silent: its zoneless target may be permanently stable and may dispatch no frame at all, which is precisely the shape this criterion forbids answering as stable. What carries the claim is extension/stability-narrator.js, where idle and cannot-tell are states of their own and stable is reachable only from an emission whose value is true, and scripts/stability-capture.test.mjs, which drives two pages in one session and requires each page's own answer with no emission of one attributed to the other. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/stability-narrator.test.mjs", whose E10 pin reads the same silent record twice to the same state and the same measurement and never lets silence alone turn a cannot-tell into stable, and node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/stability-capture.test.mjs", whose E11 drive reddens when one page's emission reaches another page's answer.
